problems.title: A stale runner-up can produce a nonmaximal assignment
problems.source_location: Algorithm 1, PDF p.7, line 7; pinned heuristics/src/gaic.rs, affinity/favorite updates
claim: Algorithm 1 requires a maximum-agreement label. In `heuristics/src/gaic.rs`, the runner-up state is updated only when the favorite changes.
analysis: After affinities become \((1,5,4)\), the cached runner-up can remain label zero. Removing two neighbors of the favorite gives \((1,3,4)\), without triggering the required rescan. Zero-temperature selection can therefore return agreement \(3\) despite an available value \(4\). This is a state-invariant failure, not a statement about every clustering run.
result: The released update can violate the maximizing assignment rule. Its frequency and benchmark impact are unknown.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: Rescan favorites after decreases, using the existing complete affinity scan and its declared tie convention. A more selective cache update needs an equivalent maintained invariant.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a local released-heuristic defect without demonstrated central approximation damage.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.

problems.title: Exact candidate scoring has an omitted quadratic cost
problems.source_location: Theorem 2.3, PDF p.6; Proposition B.1, PDF p.21; Algorithm 2, PDF p.22, line 11
claim: Theorem 2.3 states linear dependence on graph order for fixed approximation parameters; Algorithm 2 compares exact full-graph candidate agreement scores.
analysis: Two candidates such as balanced two-part and all-one assignments can differ on \(\Theta(n^2)\) edge signs. Exact comparison over arbitrary signed input requires accounting for those cross edges. Counting only sampled assignment work omits the pseudocode’s full scoring step. Approximate sampled ranking can support a separately specified randomized procedure.
result: The stated exact-scoring pseudocode is not justified by the linear runtime accounting. This does not prove that no linear-time PTAS exists.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: Include the exact scoring cost, or explicitly sample candidate scores with an error budget compatible with the approximation proof and declared random-access input model.
problems.impact_rationale: This is algorithm accounting with an alternative approximation route; impossibility of the main approximation goal is not shown.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.

problems.title: The conjecture has known subsequent author refutation
problems.source_location: The original three-quarter conjecture; authors’ MLG 2026 follow-up, Theorem 3
claim: The original \(3/4\) guarantee is labeled a conjecture; the authors’ MLG 2026 follow-up Theorem 3 refutes it.
analysis: For \(n=256\), random independent edge signs give a finite existence argument: there are at most \((2n)^{2n}\) interval-overlap patterns, while each fixed pattern’s chance of agreement above the target is bounded by \(\exp(-\binom n2/8)\). Their product is below one. This is a probabilistic existence argument, not an enumerated optimum or new discovery.

The elementary universal guarantee is \(|E|/2\): the better of all-overlapping and pairwise-disjoint interval assignments satisfies at least half the signed edges. The author follow-up limits a larger uniform constant in its stated asymptotic setting. This contextualizes known subsequent progress; it is not a repair of a falsely proved theorem.
result: A conjecture can be disproved by later work without constituting a false proof in the original paper. Historical attribution remains with the authors.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
problems.impact_rationale: This is known subsequent progress on an honestly labeled conjecture, not a supported original-paper error.
problems.existing_correction_status: The authors’ MLG 2026 follow-up explicitly refutes the conjecture; this is known follow-up, not new adoption of a local proposal.
